column1: bash/zsh: how do you put a REAL tab or newline in a string? ($'...' vs "...")
column2:
$'...'  = ANSI-C quoting — interprets backslash escapes:
  $'a\tb'  -> a<TAB>b      $'x\ny' -> two lines
  also \r \0 \e \\ \' \xHH \uHHHH
Plain "..." and '...' leave \t \n LITERAL.
$'...' does NOT expand variables ($var stays literal).

Handy:  IFS=$'\n'  (split on newlines only)
        <<< $'a\nb\nc'  (feed `read` real newlines)

column1: zsh: why does  ls *.mp3  error 'no matches found', even with &>/dev/null?
column2:
zsh NOMATCH is ON by default: a glob matching nothing raises "no matches found"
and ABORTS the command (bash instead passes the literal pattern through).
The error fires during EXPANSION — before the command/redirections run — so
&>/dev/null can't hide it.

Fixes:
  *.mp3(N)         # (N) = NULL_GLOB for this glob -> vanishes if empty (idiomatic)
  setopt null_glob # global: unmatched -> nothing
  setopt nonomatch # global: pass literal like bash
